_readme: What a provider needs FILLED IN, per wire, beyond the two boxes every
provider gets: a base URL and an API key.
Most wires need nothing here. openai, deepseek, anthropic and gemini are
all 'a URL and a bearer token', which is the default shape, so they are
deliberately absent - a wire with no entry gets the default form and that
is the whole rule. Only a wire that authenticates differently, or that
needs settings with nowhere else to live, appears below.
Each entry may set:
label      what the settings page calls this wire
help       one paragraph shown above its fields
base_url   false to hide the base URL box, or a label to rename it
key        false to hide the API key box
fields     the extra boxes, in the order they should appear
A field is:
env        THE VARIABLE NAME. Shown on the box, and the name looked up
in the real environment when the provider leaves it empty -
so a machine already exporting AWS_REGION keeps working with
nothing typed here.
label      the human name for the box (defaults to env)
help       the note under it
secret     true to mask it, with an eye to reveal - same as the key box
required   true if the provider cannot work without it
default    what it falls back to when neither the provider nor the
environment has it
placeholder  greyed-out example text
Values typed into these are saved on the provider object itself, inside
LLM_PROVIDERS in .env - NOT as loose top-level variables. That is what
lets two Bedrock providers hold two different accounts, which loose
variables cannot express. provider.py reads them through
provider_setting(), which falls back to the real environment variable of
the same name, so nothing that already works stops working.

bedrock.label: Amazon Bedrock
bedrock.help: Signs requests with AWS SigV4 rather than sending a key, so there is no URL to point at and no bearer token. Leave the credential boxes empty to use whatever this machine already has - ~/.aws/credentials, an instance role, or the AWS_* variables in the environment. Fill them in to give this provider its own account.

fields.label: region
fields.help: Which region's Bedrock endpoint to call. Models are enabled per region, so a model that works in one may not exist in another.

fields.label: profile
fields.help: A named profile out of ~/.aws/credentials. Use this OR the two keys below, not both - a profile wins if it is set.

fields.label: access key id
fields.help: Only needed if you are not using a profile or an instance role.

fields.label: secret access key
fields.help: The other half of the access key. Stored on this provider in .env.

fields.label: session token
fields.help: Only for temporary credentials (STS, SSO, an assumed role). Leave empty for long-lived keys.

claude-subscription.label: Claude subscription (Claude Code CLI)
claude-subscription.help: Spends the Claude subscription already signed in on this machine, through the Claude Agent SDK driving the claude CLI. There is no endpoint and no API key: sign in once with `claude login` in a terminal. It needs the SDK installed (pip install --user claude-agent-sdk) and needs to be able to FIND the CLI - which is what the path box below is for, because a background service does not get your shell's PATH.

fields.label: path to the claude CLI
fields.help: Leave empty to look on PATH. Set it if this provider says it can't find the CLI while `which claude` works in your terminal - a systemd service has a minimal PATH that usually leaves out ~/.local/bin, which is where npm and pipx put things.

fields.label: timeout (seconds)
fields.help: How long to wait for a reply before giving up. The CLI is slower to first token than an HTTP API because it starts a process per turn.

local.label: Local model server
local.help: An OpenAI-compatible server running on this machine or your network - LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp. Same wire as openai; the only difference is that it takes no key, so it doesn't ask for one. Its model list comes from the server's own /v1/models, so whatever you have loaded is what you can pick.
